articles.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia CEO
articles.full_content:
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

articles.title: A Beginner's Guide to Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth
articles.full_content:
A beginner's guide to Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth

We have AI at home! Set up your own free personal ChatGPT on your PC with Unsloth and Inkling or Qwen. It's private, and the whole house can use it.

By Jerry James ·

With the launch of open-weight models like Qwen, cloud-based LLM providers seem like they're more of infrastructure or appliance businesses when it comes to most routine tasks that an AI model can handle.

OpenAI and Anthropic have displayed a pattern of dropping model quality in the 'latest' version and controlling exactly what you're allowed to run on their models. Add to this ballooning costs and privacy concerns, and we get a pretty good case for moving away from this 'convenient' cloud experience.

That's basically where I was too. I wanted to offload certain token-heavy research, data collection, or coding tasks to an AI model without staring at usage limits all day. So, as any reasonable human being would do, I decided to set up my own local AI: a Claude and ChatGPT replacement that runs at home on my own hardware.

Since this was my first attempt, my primary focus was keeping it simple and hosting it on Windows. If you're a beginner, you can follow along to get one going on your home network too.

Once you have the hardware sorted, it takes about 10-15 minutes (excluding download times).

The short version

Install Unsloth Desktop, download a quantized AI model that fits your GPU's VRAM, set your context size, and turn on LAN access so everyone at home can use it.

What Do You Need to Run a Local AI at Home?

Not much (other than the hardware). Here's a short list:

  • A Windows PC with a graphics card (GPU). The more video memory (VRAM) it has, the bigger the model it can run. I'm using an RTX 5090 with 32GB VRAM for this setup.
  • Unsloth Desktop. A free app that 'serves' the AI model to you through a chat interface. Get it from Unsloth.
  • An AI model sized to fit your GPU. We'll pick one in the next section.

That's it. No terminal commands, Python environments, or subscriptions required.

Which AI Model Can Your GPU Run?

It depends on how much VRAM your graphics card has. As a rough guide, 8-12GB of VRAM handles smaller 9B-12B models, while 32GB comfortably runs 27B-35B models with plenty of room for long conversations.

On consumer-grade hardware, we'll need smaller models. The full-size Qwen model sits at around 56GB and won't really fit on a consumer graphics card unless you're running a Mac with unified memory. That's where quantization comes in.

What Is Quantization?

Quantization shrinks a model by compressing weights and moving to a lower precision. You basically trade some accuracy for a model that actually fits on your GPU and runs faster.

The same photo stored at 8, 4 and 2 bits per pixel. A model's weights lose detail the same way going from Q8 to Q4 to Q2.

If you're wondering whether this tradeoff is worth it, well, it depends. You'll find that certain types of workloads don't really care and give similar outputs, while others may be nearly unusable.

Which Model Should You Run for Your VRAM?

For this guide, we'll be going with Qwen3.8-27B with 4-bit quantization on my system with an RTX 5090. Going up a tier is an option thanks to its 32GB of VRAM, but I wanted to allow for a larger context window (how much of the conversation the model can keep in mind at once) rather than cramming in the largest model that fits.

Qwen3.8-27B at each precision with a 128K context, from our VRAM calculator. At 4-bit, the model and the context fit a 32 GB card with room to spare.

If you want to run a model of this caliber with excellent performance, a hilariously overpriced RTX 5090 (remember when $1,999 felt too high?) is unfortunately still not a terrible 'deal' these days. The other option is way more expensive enterprise-grade GPUs.

If you're on a GPU with less VRAM, you can still get something very usable going right away. The table below gives you a rough idea of where you can start.

Models marked MoE (mixture of experts) only run a few billion of their parameters for each token. They keep a decent speed on a smaller card with the rest held in system RAM, which is why a 35B model sits in the 16 GB row. On an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, our calculator puts Qwen3.6-35B at about 47 tokens per second this way.

Feel free to experiment with several models until you find one that fits your needs. You can also use GPUPartner's VRAM Calculator to get an estimate.

Can You Run Inkling 2 on an RTX 5090?

Inkling 2 Mini, yes. Inkling 2 Small, no.

Inkling 2 Mini is the newest model in this size class. Thinking Machines Lab released it on November 17, 2026: 26.4B parameters, Apache 2.0, vision support and a 1M-token context. Unsloth's recommended file, UD-Q4_K_XL, is 17.6 GB. That is within 0.1 GB of the Qwen3.8-27B file in this guide, so it sits on a 32GB card the same way and leaves about 14GB for context.

Nothing else in this guide changes. Update Unsloth Desktop first, because Inkling 2 needs a recent build, then search for Inkling 2 Mini in the same drop-down in Step 2.

Those figures are Unsloth's. They count RAM and VRAM together and cover the model alone, so a long context needs more. Inkling 2 Mini is a mixture-of-experts model with 5.4B parameters active, so the 4-bit file also runs on a 16 GB card with the remainder in system RAM, a little slower.

Inkling 2 Small is small in name only. It is a 594B model, and the smallest file Unsloth publishes is 171.7 GB. That is unified-memory territory: a 256GB Mac Studio or a DGX Station, not a graphics card.

Can You Run a Local AI on a Mac?

Yes. You'll find good alternatives in Apple's Mac lineup thanks to its unified memory. Macs are pretty good at running larger models, even if they don't offer the best performance. Just make sure you grab the MLX flavor that is custom-built for Apple Silicon.

The same trade applies to unified-memory PCs like the MSI PRO MAX EDGE AI+ 11M and NVIDIA's DGX Spark.

How Do You Set Up a Local AI with Unsloth Desktop?

It takes three steps: install Unsloth Desktop, download your model, and set the context size. I'll go over these steps in more detail below so you can follow along.

Step 1: Install Unsloth Desktop

First, we'll need a solution that 'serves' the AI model to you. My pursuit of simplicity narrowed my choices down to LM Studio or Unsloth Desktop. Both abstract away a ton of terminal commands and handle Python environments and dependencies behind a nice, simple UI, which makes them excellent picks for a first home setup.

I landed on Unsloth Desktop mostly because, well, I liked the name better. Also, it didn't try to push the very thing I was trying to escape when I opened its website: a subscription.

The community seems to like it overall too, so that's another point in its favor.

Once you've clicked through the installer and launched Unsloth, you'll see a window like this one.

Unsloth Desktop on first launch, before any model is loaded.

Step 2: Download a Quantized Model

On the top left of this main window, you can pick the model that you want to use from the drop down. We'll be using Qwen3.8-27B.

The model picker. Qwen3.8-27B is first on the Recommended list.

You should see a submenu like the one below when you click on a model. I'll be using Unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL version. The M and S versions are smaller, but the XL version behaves much closer to the full-size model without filling up our VRAM, so it seemed like a good pick for my GPU.

Every quantization of Qwen3.8-27B with its download size. The gear next to the downloaded one holds the context setting.

Step 3: Set the Context Size

Once the download completes, you should see a gear icon to the right of the model as shown in the screenshot above. Here, you can set your context size manually or leave it on Auto if you aren't sure how much you need.

I'll be setting mine to 128K (unquantized) and might reassess after I've run the model through a few of my routine tasks for a few weeks. Again, you can use this VRAM calculator to help you with these numbers for your specific GPU.

At this point, our first local AI is up and running, and you can start chatting with it right inside Unsloth.

Remember, your mileage may vary depending on your setup.

How Do You Share a Local AI Across Your Home Network?

Short answer: Unsloth Desktop has LAN sharing built in. Set a Remote password, start LAN access, and share the address it gives you with anyone on your home network.

Once Unsloth Desktop is set up with a model, you might want to give family members or friends access too. For now, we'll only serve it over our local network, so my family can use it without needing physical access to this PC.

Head into Unsloth Desktop settings (gear icon on bottom left), and look for the 'Remote & LAN' tab.

Settings, Remote & LAN. LAN access is the second card. The Remote access card above it is for a later part.

Most of this section will be greyed out until you set a Remote password. Once you've set a password, you'll see a 'Start' button for LAN access. Click that and you should see an address that anyone on your home network can open in a browser to use a local AI model within a chat interface. They'll sign in as 'unsloth' with the Remote password you set.

Just keep in mind that the PC needs to stay on with Unsloth running for anyone to reach it.

Can You Access Your Local AI Across the Internet? Soon™

Not with this setup alone. Everything so far is limited to your local home network.

If you just need a chat interface like ChatGPT, Gemini, etc. to work within your home network, you're basically done at this point! You and anyone on your network can start talking to an AI model hosted on your machine right away.

In the next parts, we'll cover performance, tunneling, as well as setting up an agent that runs locally and uses only the web tools you allow it to use. This will let you automate more complex tasks like coding, research, and so much more without being tied to a subscription or usage limits and censorship.

As always, my focus remains simplicity that allows my family to use it without too much guidance or help.

PS. If you have any recommendations for agentic harnesses or even models to try, feel free to let me know and I'll give them a go!

articles.title: XNU Linux: Full OS X GUI Userspace on Linux
articles.full_content:
Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it.

xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel module (

xnu.ko
) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (
fki.ko
).

With a stock Ubuntu kernel, 

insmod xnu.ko
boots a macOS 27 system disk made by Apple's own installer to the desktop: loginwindow, WindowServer, Dock, Finder, Safari and Chrome.

One system, two userspaces. Left: a Terminal in the hosted macOS 27.2.1 (

sw_vers
, the Darwin kernel, launchd, WindowServer, Dock and Finder running). Right: from that macOS, an SSH session into the Linux it runs inside (Ubuntu, Linux 7.0, the 
xnu
and 
fki
modules loaded, and the 
insmod xnu.ko
process the macOS kernel runs in). Straight from the hosted framebuffer, 1280×800.

The hosted desktop at the end of a 30-minute stress run, rendered on the CPU (no GPU bridge).

Safari in the hosted macOS: Wikipedia's article on XNU, kernel.org and the Linux repository on GitHub, over the hosted system's network link through Linux, with the GPU bridge on (

GPU=auto
).

Bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux 

7.0.0-1025-nvidia
): hosted macOS 27 running with 4 CPUs and 8 GiB of RAM (CPU rendering), shown over macOS Screen Sharing alongside an SSH session from the DGX Spark host into the hosted Darwin userspace.

Inside the hosted macOS on DGX Spark: About This Mac (

Chip: Unknown
, 
7.80 GB
memory, 
macOS Golden Gate 27.2
) alongside 
sysctl machdep.cpu
(
ARM processor
, 
hw.cpufamily: 0
, 
hw.ncpu: 4
) and 
hw.optional.arm
. 

      
 macOS processes (launchd, WindowServer, Safari...)    Linux processes (systemd, sshd, xnudrmd...)
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────    ────────────────────────────────────────────
 XNU (source-built, LINUX64 machine layer, kexts)  │
   ↕ linux64 host calls (xnu-patches/include/linux64_abi.h)
 xnu.ko   (APSL side: loads and runs the kernel collection)
   ↕ FKI, the foreign kernel interface (fki_*)
 fki.ko   (GPL side: CPUs, memory, faults, IPIs, files, network, host calls)
 Linux kernel (stock distro kernel, 4K pages, PAC)
  • CPUs: each hosted CPU is a Linux kernel thread pinned to a Linux CPU. XNU runs on it until it calls the host (idle, I/O, a timer); Linux keeps its own exception vectors, and 
    fki.ko
    forwards the faults and user exceptions of XNU code to XNU's handlers.
  • Memory: XNU gets one physically contiguous block from Linux (CMA) and manages it with its own pmap; XNU and Linux share the user half of the address space layout (4K pages).
  • Devices: kexts in 
    kexts/
    give macOS a disk (a file on the Linux side), a display (a framebuffer Linux reads), a keyboard and pointer, an Ethernet link (a Linux network interface), a keystore and a GPU bridge.
  • GPU: Metal in the hosted macOS runs on 
    gpu/xnu-cpu-metal
    (metal2vulkan over Vulkan). Vulkan reaches the Linux host's GPU through the DRM bridge (
    kexts/XnuDrm
    → host call → 
    gpu/xnu-drm/xnudrmd
    → the Linux render node), using Mesa's Venus driver; without a supported DRM bridge backend it falls back to Mesa lavapipe on the CPU.

Working on two arm64 Linux setups:

  • Apple Silicon Mac in an arm64 Linux VM (
    krunkit
    , 1 to 6 hosted CPUs)    :
    • macOS 27.2.1 boots to the desktop with auto-login in 31–48 s (an Apple Virtualization macOS VM on the same Mac: 49 s).
    • Apps open and quit, Spotlight and the file system work; a 30-minute stress run (40 rounds of Safari, Notes, Calculator, TextEdit, System Settings, Spotlight and a disk walk) finishes with no panic and no crash report.
    • Runs as a systemd service: started at boot, stopped cleanly with the VM, restarted after a hosted-kernel panic, each run's log kept in 
      /var/log/xnulinux/
      .
    • The GPU bridge gives hosted apps the host GPU (
      Virtio-GPU Venus (Apple M5 Max)
      ) and is enabled by default (
      GPU=auto
      ) when a virtio-gpu render node is present, falling back to CPU rendering (
      GPU=off
      ) otherwise.
  • Bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux 
    7.0.0-1025-nvidia
    )    :
    • Boots to the full macOS desktop (Screen Sharing and SSH working) directly on bare-metal arm64 Linux with 
      CPUS=4
      and 8 GiB of RAM reserved for XNU.
    • Currently renders on the CPU (Mesa lavapipe, 
      GPU=off
      ): 
      xnudrmd
      only forwards 
      virtio-gpu
      (Venus) ioctls today, so hardware GPU pass-through on the GB10 GPU requires a new DRM bridge backend.

What is still a stopgap is listed in 

docs/production.md
. Notably: the OS cryptex is merged into the system volume, AMFI is patched and SIP relaxed, and memory access is slower than a native VM (4K pages vs 16K).

  • An arm64 Linux host with PAC (
    FEAT_PAuth
    ), 4K pages, and at least 16 GB of RAM (8 GB reserved for the hosted kernel). Tested on:
    • NVIDIA DGX Spark (bare-metal Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux 
      7.0.0-1025-nvidia
      ; CPU rendering for now).
    • Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) running an arm64 Linux VM (
      krunkit
      for GPU access via virtio-gpu Venus, or 
      tart
      ).
  • A Mac with Xcode to make the system disk and build the GPU parts.
  • A macOS 27 installation (an Apple Virtualization VM disk) of your own. No Apple binaries are in this repository or distributed by it: the kexts Apple ships, the macOS system disk and its trust cache come from your own installation.
  • scripts/vm-xnu-build.sh
    (on the arm64 Linux host, once): sets up the macOS-DroidVM Linux toolchain and builds XNU (
    xnu-12377.121.6
    ) natively on arm64.
  • scripts/vm-xnu-rebuild.sh
    : applies 
    xnu-patches/
    , builds the kernel and 
    kexts/
    , and links the kernel collection with Apple's kexts from your macOS installation.
  • scripts/mk-macvm-disk.sh
    (on the Mac): turns a macOS VM disk made by Apple's installer into the hosted system's disk and copies it into the Linux VM.
  • scripts/xnulinux-boot.sh
    (on the arm64 Linux host): builds 
    fki.ko
    and 
    xnu.ko
    against the running kernel, brings up the network (and the GPU bridge when there is a render node) and boots the hosted system. Its console is 
    scripts/xnu-console.sh
    , its screen 
    tools/hosted/fb2png.py
    , input 
    tools/hosted/xnu-input.py
    . On a bare-metal host (such as a DGX Spark), set the carve-out (
    mem=
    , 
    carve_base=
    , 
    carve_mb=
    ) to fit the machine's physical memory layout, and set 
    GPU=off
    (
    xnudrmd
    supports only virtio-gpu for now).
  • scripts/install-service.sh
    (on the arm64 Linux host): runs it as 
    xnulinux.service
    , configured in 
    /etc/xnulinux.conf
    (CPUs, memory, disk, GPU). On the Mac, 
    scripts/install-krun-agent.sh
    keeps the VM itself running.
  • GPU (optional, on the Mac): 
    gpu/venus/build-darwin.sh
    builds the hosted Vulkan driver, 
    gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/
    the Metal plugin (see its README).

The Linux side and the XNU side are kept apart by license and meet only at FKI. Every source file carries an 

SPDX-License-Identifier
; the license texts are in 
LICENSES/
.

 GPL-2.0-onlyBuild, disk, boot, debugging and test tools; documentation

xnu.ko
is on the XNU side of the line: it runs XNU's code in its own address space, so it is APSL-2.0 like XNU, and Linux reports it as a non-GPL module (
MODULE_LICENSE("Proprietary")
, which taints the kernel as ZFS does). It must not include Linux headers beyond the module ABI, call Linux functions other than 
fki_*
, or carry Linux code. Upstream code (XNU, macOS-DroidVM's toolchain, Mesa, metal2vulkan, the Vulkan loader, LLVM) is fetched at pinned revisions and patched at build time; it is never committed.

  • macOS-DroidVM and UniXNU: the 4K-page XNU base, the Linux-hosted XNU toolchain, and the display, Ethernet and input kexts these are derived from.
  • metal2vulkan, Mesa (Venus, lavapipe), virglrenderer and krunkit.
  • Apple's open-source XNU.

articles.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
articles.full_content:
From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently⁠(opens in a new window), predictor) on a very large corpus of data.1

I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared⁠(opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts.

A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “an alien mind⁠”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.

The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset.2, 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.

The range of capabilities of models that are largely described by this one metric is stunning. Setting the new perplexity state-of-the-art on older datasets4, GPT‑2 was arguably the first model capable of consistently formulating coherent paragraphs of text. The next major leap, GPT‑3, was capable of learning in context, given a few examples of a task. GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT. GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models. Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics. I want to reemphasize that it was not at all clear a priori that these capabilities would appear once those precise perplexity thresholds are met—they can fundamentally be seen as emergent latent capabilities from progress on this one metric.

As AI advances very rapidly, the scope and way in which we measure downstream capabilities may change quickly. It would make little sense to evaluate GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 on most modern benchmarks; and the benchmarks used then were largely saturated around GPT‑4. In contrast, I believe looking at progress on pretraining is likely to stay informative.

A particular change in the pace of progress comes from the increasing contribution of AI to its own development. The most commonly discussed metrics revolve around AI augmenting and replacing human researchers in all stages of the development cycle; with an ultimate inflection point seen at “full recursive self-improvement”, where the process would be entirely automated with no human oversight. Apart from considering such a state as something we should obviously avoid for the sake of maintaining human control, I find this general framing misses something crucial. There is a potential step change that may come from AI participation in one key part of the development process: algorithmic research on pretraining.

We have recently witnessed unprecedented acceleration in another domain. For more than a year, we have been posing open problems in mathematics to our models as one of the ways of evaluating them. Once we upgraded to a model of log-perplexity ~0.76, it started producing groundbreaking results. For many of us that have previously worked in mathematics and adjacent fields, seeing the resolutions to questions we’ve long thought about coming out of the model one after another in a single Slack thread felt deeply surreal. Having experienced that allows us to extrapolate—such a sudden transformation is plausible in deep learning research too. While this field relies more on experimentation, there is a long history of simple insights being missed for years; and so as soon as 2027 we could conceivably see a similar avalanche of fundamental pretraining advancements5. While I expect AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining.

Given that the main way new surprising capabilities emerge is by progress on compression, a measure rooted in perplexity could give us a shared benchmark for general intelligence, regardless of the degree of automation of the development process. Extrapolating from recent progress, we should expect further transformative capabilities as we enter the ~0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window. I don’t know what those capabilities will be, and we may not be testing for them today. At the same time, we should also expect further degradation⁠(opens in a new window) in currently dominant forms of alignment auditing and further increases in evaluation and training awareness. I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards. I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors). That is, I’d like an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, measured by some key metric we can track across labs, and what concretely we’d need to achieve before going beyond it. I hope that this leads the way to a common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development.

Perplexity as a shared metric has challenges:

  • Difficulty of comparison across labs. Different developers use different evaluation datasets and train on different data mixtures. Here, we report the numbers on the main dataset we have been tracking; I believe if we establish a goal of transparency we can find transferable ways to compare the quality of different base models.

  • Detachment from actionable evaluations. Perplexity does not directly correspond to a task we care about. The reason to care about it is that we can expect advances on it to lead to emergence of entirely new capabilities.

  • Not accounting for advances outside of pretraining. Most notably, chain-of-thought reasoning does not reduce perplexity achieved by the model, even though it leads to a drastic increase in capabilities.

  • Unknown floor. We do not expect it is possible to achieve a loss of 0, which would correspond to being able to predict the dataset entirely deterministically. But we do not know what the inherent entropy of the data is. As we approach it, the apparent progress on perplexity will slow, but smaller gains on perplexity will correspond to larger leaps in model intelligence.

At the same time, perplexity has stood the test of time as a metric many research teams have put a lot of effort into optimizing, and it continues to deliver consistent gains on general intelligence. I believe it can play an important role in standardizing how we talk about AI progress, and hope to see more transparency about it across the industry.

Author

Footnotes

  • 1
  • 2
  • 3
  • 4

    Given what GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 were trained on, how well they predict code is a poor proxy for their general capabilities. This showcases a potential challenge arising from dataset selection with using perplexity as a shared metric; however it should still be informative to evaluate them jointly with modern models on general text. I chose to report perplexity on our internal codebase because I wanted to share the numbers we rely on most today to gauge progress in pretraining at OpenAI.

  • 5

    On the plot of losses of OpenAI models, you can see a steep acceleration in 2026. We attribute it mostly to the outcomes of long term research and compute investments, and only in a smaller part to automation. However, for the most recent models, we have already seen meaningful design contributions coming from AI⁠.

articles.title: The Birds of GTA 6: A Field Guide to Vice City and Leonida's Wildlife
articles.full_content:
Visit Birds Tell Us to Act on Climate page

I finished collecting the bricks of cocaine and landed my bullet-ridden seaplane at the dock. It was time for birdwatching.

A few minutes after midnight on Thursday morning, I joined millions of other gamers for the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest in the smash video game series from Rockstar Games. The new installment is already a worldwide sensation, earning more than $1.8 billion in revenue the day it was released. 

Grand Theft Auto, or GTA, games are famous for their “open worlds,” which allow players to explore massive, intricately detailed versions of America. Much of that exploration is focused on mayhem and chaos: The story missions usher players through criminal underworlds, and players are at any time free to steal cars, rob stores and pedestrians, and initiate anarchy. 

But GTA 6 has more going on than just criminality—it’s also a world filled with wildlife. Previous GTA games were set in fictionalized versions of New York City and Hollywood, but the new one returns to Vice City, its version of Miami, which was also the setting for 2002’s installment. Unlike that game, however, GTA 6’s South Florida is complete with dozens of species of birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, mammals, and other creatures. The in-game Progress menu tracks all kinds of items to find, including 338 vehicles, 205 weapons, and, of primary interest to me, at least 60 bird species. 

I made it my mission to find them all as quickly as possible.

(Side note: Pre-release marketing for GTA 6 touted 62 bird species, but the official birds Progress screen only lists 60, with a handful of others listed on the hunting screen.)

I am one hour in and I’ve found 16/60 birds https://t.co/81x42O1BuY

— The Birdist (@TheBirdist) November 19, 2026

You begin the game as Jason, a low-level criminal working to raise money to support his young family. You’re equipped with zoom binoculars before the very first mission—tracking drug runners through a swamp and escaping with the seaplane—and I used them immediately, stopping mid-lurk to scan some Double-crested Cormorants on a dock. (Distracted from the job at hand to look at birds—just like real life!) They looked like Double-crested Cormorants!

After the first mission the player is free to explore the entirety of the map, stealing cars, robbing stores, or just birding wherever they want. The game makes birding easy: Looking at any bird through the in-game binoculars gives players the option to hold a button to “study” it, thereby adding it to the Progress menu. Simply standing on the back deck of Jason’s first safehouse yields a bunch of species like Brown Pelican and Laughing Gull. It’s just like being in South Florida!

Looking south from the back deck, I spotted another bird perched on an adjacent dock, with a few people gathered at the end. Looking through my binoculars I spotted my first Herring Gull—and noticed that the people, a woman and three men, were fully and visibly naked. Jason apparently lives next to a nudist resort. It’s just like being in South Florida!

Two down, 58 to go. I found a few more species right in Jason’s backyard, including American Crow, House Sparrow, and South Florida-appropriate Monk Parakeets, before venturing out into the huge map. My strategy for finding birds in GTA 6 was the same as finding birds in real life: look in as many habitats as I could find. I started by “borrowing” a fanboat off a nearby dock and heading back to the swampy areas near the seaplane mission. There were tons of birds across the open water and in the marsh: Caspian Terns, Mottled Ducks, Sanderlings, Spotted Sandpipers, Great Blue Herons, Glossy and White Ibis, and … flocks of Whooping Cranes?

incredibly healthy populations of critically-endangered Whooping Cranes across Vice City. Huge if true. https://t.co/doe6oMOvBX

— The Birdist (@TheBirdist) November 19, 2026

In fact, I found a number of avian inaccuracies in just my first few hours of playtime. Certain species like Whooping Crane and Red-cockaded Woodpecker are common throughout the map, despite being endangered and threatened, respectively, in real life. Golden Eagles are extremely rare in Florida, but I found one soaring over the Mt. Kalaga area (mountains, one may point out, aren’t found in Florida either). Some species have confusing naming quirks—the chickadee is Black-capped instead of Carolina, and there’s a “New World Oriole” instead of a Baltimore Oriole—but those changes are likely due to the fact that Carolina and Baltimore don’t exist in the GTA universe.


Though some of the inaccuracies may feel like a letdown in a game that is being hailed as the Greatest of All Time, I think it’s important to remember that it’s also game where you can get a ride from a dog driving a jet ski. Grand Theft Auto games are meant to be fun, not science. Plus, despite some of the misfires, the avifauna feels well thought-out. The map is true to the ecological boundaries of South Florida, with herons, gulls, and other waterbirds in the south while birds like Red-bellied Woodpecker, Wood Stork, and American Robin are found farther north. Birders know that certain exotic species have made their home in tropical South Florida, including Spot-breasted Oriole and Red Junglefowl, both in the game.

That geographic fidelity is the main tip for anyone looking to check off all the game’s birds: Find their habitat. The game doesn’t tell you what species to look for, so you’ll need to cover a lot of ground to find everything. Wading birds, shorebirds, and seabirds are common in the southern coastal part of the map. A number of smaller, open-country or forest birds are found up north. Owls come out at night. Birds in zoos and domestic farmyard birds count towards the 60, too, so don’t overlook those areas.

Wild Boar roadkill. It’s just like birding in Florida! https://t.co/gT84IticOK

— The Birdist (@TheBirdist) November 19, 2026

The most accurate aspect is the actual landscape. Having birded extensively across South Florida myself, the habitats are immediately recognizable, from the pebbly mangrove beaches at the Keys to the grassy swamps further north. The setting feels absolutely real, from the fonts on the roadside fruit stands to the roadkill alongside the highways. (I found dead wild boar and dead deer by the side of the road, and a Turkey Vulture somehow flew into a building I was in and died at my feet.) 
So, if you’re up for the kind of funhouse-mirror version of Florida that the game presents, you can have a blast, and adding birdwatching into the insane free-for-all makes for some delightful moments. This guy just wanted to look at a gull but ended up chucking a woman off a pier. I’ve made myself laugh out loud by screeching to a halt in the middle of busy highways or intersections and jumping out of my car to look for birds while motorist behind me scream and swear. I love it.

easily my favorite thing to do so far is just screech to a halt in the middle of a busy intersection and start birding https://t.co/QsDOLmNfYq

— The Birdist (@TheBirdist) November 19, 2026

As I was dodging dirt-biking rednecks to look for species in a northerly forest, I couldn’t help but compare birding in GTA 6 to birding in Red Dead Redemption 2 (RDR2), the latest installment in Rockstar’s other huge franchise. Birds and birding are presented quite similarly in both games, including the binocular “study” mechanic and many of the same species, but the experiences are totally different. RDR2 was set in the late 1800s, and players rode on horseback or locomotive through a comparatively wide-open and untrammeled version of America. There was mayhem in that game, too—outlaw gangs and marauders—but there were many peaceful moments, too, when a player could look out across wild landscape with nothing but nature as a soundtrack.

Not so in GTA 6. There’s plenty of birdsong on the soundtrack, but it competes with an endless racket of car radios, revving engines, swearing pedestrians, and blaring horns. There’s garbage almost everywhere, lapping the shorelines and blowing along the streets. There seems to be no inch of landscape in GTA 6 that hasn’t been lessened by the touch of humans. It is, I have to admit, a realistic depiction of birding in South Florida.

Birders working to fill out their GTA VI wildlife checklists should know something I just found out: THERE’S A ZOO https://t.co/2xN0joPKcR

— The Birdist (@TheBirdist) November 20, 2026

Though GTA 6 provides what feels the most accurate version of modern birding ever put to screen, obsessing over the realism misses the point of having fun. Birders can, and should, visit the real South Florida to find the actual birds depicted in the game (and many more), but they can’t do it while also jumping over broken highway bridges on a stolen motorcycle. Birding is a bonus in GTA 6; mayhem is the draw.

I played for two hours after midnight, then about six straight hours Thursday before having to call it quits to write this column. In that time I found 50 of the 60 species listed in the “birds” compendium. I jumped back in this morning before work and found a huge chunk of species at a zoo (makes sense!) and on a farm, then found the 60th and final, an American Barn Owl, on a water tank in a town in the north of the map. Success! 

The biggest thing I can confirm is that all 60 birds on this list are available immediately, without needing any story progression. In Red Dead Redemption 2, some bird species were only found in Guarma, only accessible later in the game

— The Birdist (@TheBirdist) November 20, 2026


I felt a wave of satisfaction, and while I’m not certain if I was the first one to find them all, when I posted about it, a Rockstar designer replied with, “History!” I’d met my goal, and celebrated in a way that only Grand Theft Auto games allow: by driving my car full speed off a cliff into the ocean.

articles.title: Ramp in talks to raise $1B+ at more than $70B valuation (2 minute read)

articles.title: TPG to take BILL private in $6B deal with Corpay (3 minute read)
articles.summary: TPG and Corpay agreed to acquire BILL Holdings for about $6 billion in cash, offering $63.25 per share, a 31% premium to BILL's 60-day volume-weighted average price before takeover reports emerged. Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for roughly one-third of BILL and retain an option to buy the rest in 2030, while the deal follows activist pressure, workforce cuts, and intensifying competition in SMB financial software.
